quiz.title: Integration by Parts Quiz (Exercise 7.6)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on integration by parts, the ILATE rule and the standard integrals from Exercise 7.6. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths integration by parts

questions.q: Integration by parts is derived from which rule?
questions.explanation: Integrating the product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv' and rearranging gives ∫u v' dx = uv − ∫u' v dx, which is integration by parts.

questions.q: In the ILATE rule, which function is chosen as the first function (u)?
options: The one that comes later in ILATE
The one that comes earlier in ILATE
questions.explanation: ILATE orders Inverse, Logarithmic, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential. The function appearing earlier is taken as u (the part to differentiate).
Take u = x, dv = e^x dx. Then ∫ x e^x dx = x e^x − ∫ e^x dx = x e^x − e^x + C = e^x(x − 1) + C.

options: x cos x − sin x + C
x sin x + cos x + C
questions.explanation: Take u = x, dv = sin x dx, so v = −cos x. Then ∫ x sin x dx = −x cos x + ∫ cos x dx = −x cos x + sin x + C.
Here ln x is Logarithmic, so u = ln x, dv = x dx, v = x^2/2. Then ∫ x ln x dx = (x^2/2) ln x − ∫(x^2/2)(1/x) dx = (x^2/2) ln x − x^2/4 + C.

questions.q: Which integral matches the form ∫ e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] dx?
questions.explanation: The standard result is ∫ e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] dx = e^x f(x) + C, since the derivative of e^x f(x) is exactly e^x[f(x) + f'(x)].
Write ln x as (ln x)(1). Take u = ln x, dv = dx, v = x. Then ∫ ln x dx = x ln x − ∫ x(1/x) dx = x ln x − x + C.

questions.q: Using ∫ e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] dx = e^x f(x) + C, evaluate ∫ e^x(sin x + cos x) dx.
questions.explanation: Here f(x) = sin x and f'(x) = cos x, so the integral is e^x sin x + C.

faq.q: When should I use integration by parts?
faq.a: Use it when the integrand is a product of two different types of functions — for example x times e^x, or x times sin x, or x times ln x. It rewrites ∫u v' dx as uv − ∫u' v dx so the remaining integral is simpler.

faq.q: What does the ILATE rule tell you?
faq.a: ILATE (Inverse, Logarithmic, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential) is the order for choosing the first function u. Whichever function appears earlier in ILATE is taken as u and differentiated; the other is integrated. This keeps the second integral easier.

faq.q: Why is ln x integrated by parts when it looks like a single function?
faq.a: Write ln x as the product (ln x)(1). Take u = ln x and dv = dx. Applying integration by parts gives x ln x − x + C. The same trick works for inverse trigonometric functions like sin⁻¹ x.

faq.q: What is the special formula ∫ e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] dx?
faq.a: When an integrand has e^x multiplied by a function plus its own derivative, the answer is simply e^x f(x) + C. Spotting this pattern saves a full round of integration by parts and appears often in Exercise 7.6.
